When it blatantly favors one customer
When it offers a discount to customers in exchange for advertising space
correct: When it is offered to only a few customers
When it blatantly favors one customer
why: Under the Robinson-Patman Act, advertising allowances must be offered to all competing customers on proportionally equal terms, so allowances limited to a few customers or that blatantly favor one are illegal.
feynman: It's like a teacher handing out extra credit: it's fair if every student gets the same chance, but not if only a few students, or just one favorite, are allowed to earn it.

question: Multiple Choice Questlon quantity discount is based on the amount of merchandise bought during a certain span of time and most often involves more than one transaction.
why: A cumulative quantity discount is tied to the total amount bought over a period of time, usually across several orders.
feynman: It's like a coffee shop punch card, where the more drinks you buy over several weeks, the bigger your reward gets.

question: Multiple Choice Questlon What is a slotting allowance?
choices: A discount based on the number of products purchased
A discount for retailers who feature a particular product in their ads
A price reduction offered to business customers who pay their bills promptly
A fee paid to a retailer to place a new product on store shelves
correct: A fee paid to a retailer to place a new product on store shelves
why: A slotting allowance is a payment a manufacturer makes to a retailer for shelf space, usually to launch a new product.
feynman: It's like paying a store a fee so your new snack gets a spot on the shelf where shoppers will see it.

question: Every six months, a local hardware store receives a cumulative quantity discount on the tools it buys from Ace Tool Manufacturing. Which of the following is likely true?
choices: The more tools the hardware store buys, the more the discount will increase.
The store will offer special bargains to its customers two times a year.
The store cannot offer special prices to its customers except at the end of the discount period.
The store has a sales goal or quota for each six-month sales period.
correct: The more tools the hardware store buys, the more the discount will increase.
The store will offer special bargains to its customers two times a year.
The store has a sales goal or quota for each six-month sales period.

question: Multiple Select Questlon Slotting allowances are considered unethical by some people for which of the following reasons?
choices: They place large manufacturers at a competitive disadvantage.
Large slotting allowances could be considered bribery.
They are too expensive relative to the benefits they provide.
Small manufacturers are not able to afford them which puts them at a competitive disadvantage.
correct: Large slotting allowances could be considered bribery.
Small manufacturers are not able to afford them which puts them at a competitive disadvantage.
why: Critics say big slotting payments look like bribery of the retailer and that small manufacturers cannot afford them, which puts them at a competitive disadvantage.
feynman: It's like paying a store to put your lemonade stand at the front of the mall: a big payment looks like a bribe, and a kid with little money can't compete with the rich company.

question: Multiple Choice Questlon quantity discount is based on how much the customer buys in a single order.
why: A noncumulative quantity discount is calculated separately on each individual order, which matches the question's "single order" wording.
feynman: It's like getting a discount at the store only for the big box you carry to the register today, no matter what you bought last week.

question: Multiple Choice Questlon discount. When a price is reduced because a large amount of a product is being purchased, it is called a
why: A quantity discount is a reduction in the base price given when a buyer purchases a set amount of merchandise.
feynman: It's like buying a big box of cereal that costs less per box than buying one box at a time.

question: Multiple Select Questlon In March, before most consumers begin shopping for summer products, a shoe factory offers retailers a seasonal discount on sandals. What are the purposes of this pricing tactic? Select all the correct options.
choices: To build consumer excitement about the coming summer sales season
To move inventory out ofthe factory as soon as possible
To expand the summer buying season into early spring
To make it easier to plan the factory's production schedule
correct: To move inventory out ofthe factory as soon as possible
To make it easier to plan the factory's production schedule
why: A seasonal discount rewards retailers for ordering early, which clears the factory's inventory and lets the factory plan its production schedule.
feynman: It's like a bakery giving a discount if you pre-order cookies early, so the baker knows how many to bake and doesn't have a pile of cookies sitting around.

question: Puffery is illegal in advertising.
why: Puffery is exaggerated, subjective opinion that cannot be checked as fact, so it is generally legal and not actionable as false advertising.
feynman: Saying "best pizza in town" is like bragging that your dad is the strongest, which is just a boast and not a lie anyone can prove wrong.

question: Multiple Choice Questlon discount encourages retailers to continue buying from the same supplier because, if they switch, they might lose the discount
why: A cumulative quantity discount applies to total purchases over a period, so it rewards loyalty and gives buyers a reason not to switch suppliers.
feynman: It's like a coffee shop punch card where every purchase adds up to a free drink, so you keep going back instead of starting over somewhere else.

question: Multiple Select Questlon Which of the following are considered deceptive reference prices?
why: Deceptive reference pricing means showing a made-up ("fictitious") or artificially raised ("inflated") original price so a discount looks bigger than it really is.
feynman: It's like a store putting a fake high sticker on a toy and crossing it out so you think you're getting a big deal.

question: Multiple Choice Questlon Each time Eddie's Cars sells a vehicle, the company receives a larger discount from the manufacturer. At the end of the fiscal year, the company often slashes its prices by several hundred dollars per car because that amount will be more than offset by the increased discount the company receives from the manufacturer. The manufacturer is giving Eddie's Cars
why: The discount grows with each vehicle sold over the year, which is how a cumulative quantity discount works, rewarding total purchases over a period.
feynman: It's like a frequent-buyer card where each purchase earns a bigger reward the more you've bought over the whole year.

question: Multiple Choice Questlon quantity discount encourages the customer to buy more product immediately.
why: A noncumulative quantity discount applies to a single purchase, so the buyer has to order more at once to get it.
feynman: It's like a store giving you a deal only if you fill your cart today, rather than a deal you earn slowly over many trips.

question: Multiple Choice Questlon Which pricing tactic lowers the price below store cost?
why: Loss-leader pricing sets a product's price at or below the store's cost to draw shoppers in so they buy other, higher-margin items.
feynman: It's like a lemonade stand giving away cups for free so lots of kids come over and buy your cookies.

question: Multiple Choice Questlon The pricing tactic where a shipper charges one rate for all customers, regardless of their location, is called pricing.
why: Uniform delivered pricing (also called single-zone or postage stamp pricing) charges every customer the same freight cost regardless of distance from the dispatch point.
feynman: It's like a postage stamp, where a letter costs the same whether it goes next door or across the country.

question: Multiple Choice Questlon Which of the following would most likely be a loss-leader pricing tactic?
choices: Receive a discount on a hotel room during the off season.
Buy one box of cereal at the regular price, get one free.
Enjoy reduced prices on pink heart-shaped boxes of candy after Valentine's Day.
Get a bigger manufacturer discount each time your dealership sells another car.
correct: Buy one box of cereal at the regular price, get one free.
why: A loss leader is a product sold at or below cost to draw shoppers in, and a grocery item like cereal on a deep promotion fits that, while the other choices are seasonal or quantity discounts.
feynman: It is like a lemonade stand handing out cheap cookies so people walk over and buy lots of other things.

question: Multiple Choice Questlon In the United States, it is considered unethical and illegal for advertisements to the consumer so much that the person is harmed.
why: U.S. advertising law (FTC) prohibits deceptive advertising that misleads consumers to their detriment, so "deceive" is the term that fits.
feynman: Ads are allowed to try to convince you to buy something, but they can't trick you with lies, like a friend who tells you a fake story to get your lunch money.

question: Multiple Choice Questlon A firm sets extremely low prices for its products so that most customers will stop shopping elsewhere. This will cause other companies to go out of business and leave the firm with no more competition. The firm has engaged in
why: Predatory pricing is setting prices very low, often below cost, to drive rivals out of business and leave the firm with no competition.
feynman: It's like a lemonade stand giving away lemonade for free until every other stand on the street closes, then raising the price once it's the only one left.

question: Multiple Choice Questlon A national retail chain has signs throughout its stores that say: "Sale! 50% off our regular price!" Journalists investigate and discover that the company has never sold any merchandise at what it calls its regular price. What type of activity is this firm engaging in?
why: Advertising a discount from a "regular price" that was never actually charged is a fake reference price, which is deceptive reference pricing.
feynman: It's like a store putting a made-up $100 tag on a shirt it always sold for $50 and then shouting "half off!", so the deal isn't real.

question: Multiple Choice Questlon Which of the following is correct with respect to predatory pricing?
choices: It is outlawed by the Sherman Act and Federal Trade Commission Act.
It promotes cartels among firms in the market
It promotes diversity in the marketplace.
correct: It is outlawed by the Sherman Act and Federal Trade Commission Act.
why: Predatory pricing (pricing below cost to drive out rivals) is an anticompetitive practice prohibited under Section 2 of the Sherman Act and enforced by the FTC under Section 5 of the FTC Act.
feynman: It's like a big store selling stuff at a loss until every small shop closes, then raising prices, and the government has rules against that kind of bullying.

question: Multiple Select Questlon Every six months, a local hardware store receives a cumulative quantity discount on the tools it buys from Ace Tool Manufacturing. Which of the following is likely true?
choices: The store will offer special bargains to its customers two times a year.
The store has a sales goal or quota for each six-month sales period.
The more tools the hardware store buys, the more the discount will increase.
The store cannot offer special prices to its customers except at the end of the discount period.
correct: The store will offer special bargains to its customers two times a year.
The store has a sales goal or quota for each six-month sales period.
The more tools the hardware store buys, the more the discount will increase.
why: A cumulative quantity discount grows with total purchases over a set period (here six months), which implies a per-period purchasing or sales target and a pattern of twice-yearly promotions.
feynman: It's like a frequent-buyer card where the more you buy before the card resets, the bigger your reward, so you set a goal for each round and run sales when the round ends.

question: Multiple Choice Questlon Which of the following terms describes a firm's actions when it sells the same product to different resellers at different prices?
why: Price discrimination means charging different buyers different prices for the same product, and the price gap isn't explained by cost differences.
feynman: It's like a lemonade stand charging one neighbor $1 and another neighbor $2 for the exact same cup.

question: Multiple Choice Questlon pricing, where items are sold at a price below the store's cost. Some states require some minimum markup and prohibit
why: Loss-leader pricing means selling selected goods below cost to attract shoppers, and minimum markup laws ban exactly that.
feynman: It's like a lemonade stand selling cups for less than the lemons cost just to get people to come over, and the law says you can't do that.

question: Multiple Choice Questlon Price fixing is the illegal tactic of cooperating with other firms to prices.
why: Price fixing is competing firms agreeing to set prices artificially instead of letting the market decide them.
feynman: It's like all the lemonade stands on your street secretly agreeing to charge the same price, so nobody has to compete for customers.

question: Multiple Choice Questlon A representative of a cosmetics company is determined to undercut rivals and win a prize for selling the most products door-to-door. To boost sales, the seller slashes prices below the cost of buying products from the manufacturer. What activity is this salesperson engaged in?
why: Loss-leader pricing is selling items below cost to attract customers and boost sales, which matches this seller pricing under the manufacturer's cost.
feynman: It is like a lemonade stand that sells cups for less than the lemons cost just to get a big crowd and beat the stand next door.

question: Multiple Choice Questlon Which of the following does the Sherman Antitrust Act address?
why: The Sherman Antitrust Act bans agreements that restrain trade, and price fixing among competitors is the standard example.
feynman: It is like two rival lemonade stands secretly agreeing to charge the same high price so you have no cheaper choice.

question: Multiple Choice Questlon Using predatory pricing, a firm sets a very low price for one or more of its products with the goal of
choices: driving up the value of the company's stock
driving its competition out of business
making its annual sales report look better
capturing market share with competitive advantage
correct: driving its competition out of business
why: Predatory pricing means setting prices very low, often below cost, to force rivals out of the market so the firm can later earn higher profits.
feynman: It's like a big lemonade stand giving lemonade away so the kids' stands nearby go broke, then raising the price once they're gone.

question: Multiple Choice Questlon A small, isolated community has only four auto mechanics. They drink together in the local bar, where they all agree to charge the same inflated price for their services. When cars break down, customers have no choice but to pay whatever the mechanics ask. The mechanics are engaging in
why: Competitors at the same level of the market (the four mechanics) who agree to charge the same price are engaging in horizontal price fixing.
feynman: It's like four lemonade stands on one street secretly agreeing to all charge $10 so nobody can pick a cheaper one.

question: Predatory pricing is illegal for which of the following reasons?
choices: It drives most competition out of business and leaves the market in the control of only a few companies.
It unfairly bundles together lower-quality products.
It involves deceiving customers and then selling them a more expensive product.
It is an unfair method of competition.
correct: It drives most competition out of business and leaves the market in the control of only a few companies.
It is an unfair method of competition.

question: Price discrimination is illegal under all conditions.
why: Price discrimination is unlawful only when it harms competition, and defenses such as cost justification and good-faith meeting of a competitor's price make some forms legal.
feynman: It's like a store giving a bigger discount to someone who buys a hundred cookies, which is fair because it costs the store less per cookie, so it isn't always against the rules.

question: Multiple Choice Questlon What is the key characteristic of vertical price fixing?
choices: Prices are taken out of the decision-making process for consumers
Prices rise as the cost of living rises
The parties who collude are at the same level of various marketing channels
The parties who collude are at different levels of the same marketing channels
correct: The parties who collude are at different levels of the same marketing channels
why: Vertical price fixing is an agreement among parties at different levels of the same distribution chain, such as a manufacturer and a retailer, to set prices.
feynman: It's like a cereal maker and a grocery store secretly agreeing on the price you'll pay, even though they sit at different steps of the same path from factory to shelf.

question: Multiple Choice Questlon What term describes scheming with other companies to control prices?
why: Price fixing is an agreement among competing companies to set, raise, or stabilize prices instead of competing on them.
feynman: It's like all the lemonade stands on your street secretly agreeing to charge $5 so none of them has to lower the price to win customers.

question: Multiple Choice Questlon What is a manufacturer's suggested retail price (MSRP)?
choices: A price set by manufacturers to pressure retailers to sell the product at that price
A fee paid to a retailer to get a product onto its shelves
A price that includes shipping and handling costs for the purchase
An illegal discount offered by a manufacturer to some retailers but not others
correct: A price set by manufacturers to pressure retailers to sell the product at that price
why: MSRP is the price a manufacturer recommends that retailers charge, which keeps selling prices consistent across stores, and choice A is the closest match.
feynman: It's like a toy company printing a "should cost $20" sticker on the box, so every store knows what price the maker wants.

question: Multiple Choice Questlon Which piece of legislation governs price fixing in the United States?
why: Section 1 of the Sherman Antitrust Act of 1890 bans agreements among competitors to fix prices, and courts treat these agreements as automatically illegal.
feynman: If all the lemonade stands on a street secretly agree to charge the same high price, they are cheating customers, and the Sherman Act is the old rule that says they can't do that.

question: Multiple Select Questlon Which of the following occur under horizontal price fixing?
choices: Price becomes the focus of the decision-making process for consumers.
Business rivals that produce and sell the same type of merchandise collude with each other.
One firm controls the production and distribution of a product from beginning to end.
Price is eliminated as an influence on the consumer's decision-making process.
correct: Business rivals that produce and sell the same type of merchandise collude with each other.
Price is eliminated as an influence on the consumer's decision-making process.
why: Horizontal price fixing is an agreement among direct competitors at the same level to set prices, which takes price out of the competitive choice consumers make.
feynman: If all the lemonade stands on your street secretly agree to charge the same price, you can't pick the cheaper one, so price stops mattering when you choose.
